info.bio: Banda inglesa de post-grunge formada en 1992. Su álbum de debut fue Sixteen Stone, en 1994. Llamados Bush por el distrito londinense de Sheperd's Bush. En 1996 estrenaron su segundo álbum, Razorblade Suitcase, en el que se observan sus primeros coqueteos con la electrónica. De éste álbum se editaría una versión de remezclas titulada Deconstructed al año siguiente. En 1999 se edita su tercer álbum de estudio, The Science of Things, cuyas ventas comienzan a no responder a las espectativas creadas por sus dos álbumes anteriores.

scenes.name: Los rockers de garaje
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: En 1966 no tenían nombre (Billboard los llamaba «rockers»); hoy se les llama grupos de garaje. La respuesta creativa americana a la invasión británica: chicos blancos de suburbio que ensayaban en el garaje familiar y tocaban en gimnasios, iglesias y fiestas, con cortes de pelo de Brian Jones, actitud de Jagger, fuzz, rave-ups a lo Yardbirds, Them y Stones y, casi siempre, un órgano Farfisa o Vox con un regusto siniestro de película de terror de autocine. Recuperaban la línea del rock americano de 1963-1964 (Kingsmen, Trashmen) que los Beatles cortaron en seco: «Hanky Panky» de Tommy James, grabado en 1963, fue número 1 en julio de 1966. Ese septiembre las listas se llenaron de discos duros: «96 Tears» de ? and the Mysterians (mexicanoamericanos de Flint, con un órgano hipnótico de otro disco), «Dirty Water» de los Standells, «You’re Gonna Miss Me» de los 13th Floor Elevators y «Psychotic Reaction» de Count Five, calco del «I’m a Man» de los Yardbirds. Quejas dirigidas a las mujeres, pero también una nueva confianza; quejas pequeñas que empezaban a encontrar un objetivo, como en «One of These Days» de los Roosters.

scenes.name: Grunge
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El grunge, revival del hard rock de los setenta y renacimiento musical de Seattle, fue uno de los grandes fenómenos de los noventa (casi solo en EE UU). Green River lo inauguran (Come On Down) y Pearl Jam, Soundgarden, Melvins y Mudhoney fijan sus cuatro puntos cardinales; Nirvana, con Nevermind, lo convierten en una tragaperras y en la banda sonora de la crisis nerviosa de una generación. Después, Alice In Chains (Dirt), Foo Fighters, Hammerbox, GodHeadSilo, Everclear, Stone Temple Pilots, Tool (el grupo más innovador de la segunda generación: Aenima, Lateralus), God Machine, Helmet, Quicksand, Urge Overkill, los Smashing Pumpkins (Siamese Dream, Mellon Collie), Scarce, Creed, Bush, Manic Street Preachers, Silverchair.

podcast.title: The Crow: City of Angels Soundtrack Contribution (1996)
podcast.body: Bush was featured on the soundtrack for *The Crow: City of Angels*, the 1996 sequel to *The Crow*. This collection was considered "pretty much as good as the first one" and included other prominent bands of the era. "Bush, Corn, Deftones, E-Pop, White Zombie, Filter."

podcast.body: This band saw crossover airplay on active rock radio stations, helping the format become less of a niche. "But there was also some crossover with alternative rock stations, offspring, food fighters, bush and so on."

srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 2: The Role of Indie Rock

podcast.title: Artist Philosophy on Performance and Creation
podcast.body: Rossdale's artistic philosophy centers on pouring maximum effort into making the best possible record, free from commercial expectations or statistical pressures. He performs every live show with the intensity of it being his last, maintaining the same energy and intention for audiences of 400 or 40,000, believing this commitment is vital for an artist's longevity and to earn audience support. "The main thing my only job and my only concern is to pour over that record and make it the best that I can so that if God forbid, somebody takes this time and doesn't do the whole thing on speakers with somebody else, they can enjoy it together."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Bush: The Post-CD Band  Featuring Gavin Rossdale

podcast.title: Career Transition from 90s Rock Star to Indie Musician
podcast.body: Gavin Rossdale's journey with Bush exemplifies the transition from multi-platinum success in the 1990s to adapting to the contemporary, post-CD music business. He consciously embraced the new realities, including digital distribution and self-funding, as a means to continue making music. "How can a musician who enjoyed multi-platinum glory days in the 1990s adjust to the new realities of the music business today?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Bush: The Post-CD Band  Featuring Gavin Rossdale

podcast.title: Departure from Interscope and Self-Funding
podcast.body: Rossdale made a proactive decision to leave Interscope after a conversation with Jimmy Iovine, opting to fund his album "Sea of Memories" himself rather than wait to be "tapped on the shoulder." Interscope was generous in providing previous recordings, but the bulk of the album's setup and execution was a personal investment. "I had a conversation with Jimmy and I wanted to leave before I was tapped on the shoulder into whatever."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Bush: The Post-CD Band  Featuring Gavin Rossdale

podcast.title: Early Career Gamble and Indispensability Avoidance
podcast.body: In his early career, Rossdale deliberately chose menial labor jobs that paid no more than $50 a day and where he could not become indispensable. This strategic choice was made to prevent any alternative career path from becoming too enticing and diverting him from his primary goal of pursuing music, a significant gamble that ultimately paid off. "Every job I did was only mean your labor and it was only in places where I knew that they would never, I could not become indispensable."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Bush: The Post-CD Band  Featuring Gavin Rossdale

podcast.title: Embracing Digital Consumption and Streaming
podcast.body: Rossdale actively uses Spotify Premium and purchases music from Beatport for harder-to-find tracks, acknowledging the collective effort required in the new music ecosystem. He views streaming as "absolutely incredible" for fostering interest and providing instant access to music. "So I fully embraced the way that music is now, and I have my Spotify premium."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Bush: The Post-CD Band  Featuring Gavin Rossdale

podcast.title: Entrepreneurial Approach and Personal Label
podcast.body: Rossdale has adopted an entrepreneurial mindset, effectively running his own music business with the assistance of managers and distribution deals. The release of his 2014 album "Man On the Run" on his personal label, Zoomer Rock Records, signifies a return to the independent artist model, reminiscent of his early career. "So you've turned into a real entrepreneur. You're doing things, you're running your own business essentially right now with help from a couple of managers and you've got a distribution deal and that's the thing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Bush: The Post-CD Band  Featuring Gavin Rossdale

podcast.title: Featured on Big Shiny Toons 2
podcast.body: Bush was among the artists featured on Much Music's *Big Shiny Toons 2* compilation CD. Released in 1997, this 100% alt-rock track listing helped the album sell over 1.2 million units in Canada, underscoring the genre's significant popularity. "featuring the prodigy, blur, Marilyn Manson, Bush, Collective Soul, the Tea Party, Radiohead, Stone Temple Pilots, and more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Future of the Music Video - Part 2

podcast.title: First-Person Lyrical Approach
podcast.body: Bush was cited as an example of a Post-Grunge band, characteristic for employing a "first person approach" in their lyrics, which differed significantly from the metaphorical lyrical framing common in Grunge music. "Now think about the lyrical writing style of collective soul or bush or third eye blind and matchbox 20. You see what I mean?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mentorship Role on The Voice
podcast.body: Gavin Rossdale served as a mentor on "The Voice," recognizing it as an "incredibly gracious platform" to promote his new record. He appreciated the hard work and discipline demonstrated by the aspiring singers, noting their different path compared to the traditional pub/club circuit he experienced. "You're a mentor on the voice. What does that mean? It means an incredibly gracious platform with which to announce that I have a new record."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Bush: The Post-CD Band  Featuring Gavin Rossdale

podcast.title: Pledge Music for Fan Engagement
podcast.body: Bush utilized Pledge Music as a crowdfunding platform, not primarily for financing, but to generate excitement and anticipation for new releases. This strategy helps to navigate a fragmented media landscape by directly engaging fans and ensuring awareness, compensating for the decline of traditional promotional channels like MTV or numerous alternative radio stations. "pledge music is an incredible company. This solely set up to create excitement and anticipation that we used to get when there was incredible, at least we were, I mean, I'm going to talk about America and other than the encounter, we did so great and many more stations than there are now."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Bush: The Post-CD Band  Featuring Gavin Rossdale

podcast.title: Producer Steve Albini's Work
podcast.body: The legendary producer Steve Albini, who recorded Mono's *Hymn to the Immortal Wind* album, is known for his work on albums with Bush. "This is from a 2009 album entitled Him to the Immortal Wind, which is a big fan favorite and recorded by the legendary Steve Elbeni, who did all those albums with Nirvana and the Pixies and the Breeders and Bush."

podcast.title: Secret Love Child Daisy Lowe – DNA Confirmed 15 Years Later, Gavin Already Her Godfather
podcast.body: In the 1980s, Gavin Rossdale had a fling with British fashion designer Pearl Lowe. They broke up, and Pearl later gave birth to a daughter named Daisy. The question of paternity was uncertain, and Gavin was not initially suspected. Gavin was asked to be Daisy's godfather and accepted — meaning he was the godfather of his own biological child. It was not until the autumn of 2004, approximately 15 years after Daisy's birth, that Pearl persuaded Gavin to take a DNA test, which confirmed he was the father. The revelation put strain on his relationship with wife Gwen Stefani, while Pearl's then-boyfriend Danny Goffey of Supergrass also had to be informed. At age 18, Daisy posed nude in the magazine *ID*. "Gavin Rossdale is actually the father of his goddaughter."
